uses.context: Recent foundation models support two distinct solutions. INSID3 constructs a mask from frozen DINOv3 features through debiasing, clustering, and similarity aggregation~\cite{insid3,dinov3}. CG-ICS generates language concepts from the reference, evaluates and searches these concepts, and combines them with visual prompts in SAM~3~\cite{cgics,sam3}. Their central difference is how the reference becomes actionable evidence: direct visual correspondence in one system, and concept-guided segmentation supported by visual transfer in the other.

uses.context: Reference-conditioned segmentation builds on one-shot prediction~\cite{oslsm}, support prototypes~\cite{panet}, and dense support--query correspondence~\cite{hsnet}. Visual in-context learning broadens this idea by expressing tasks through image examples: visual prompting casts prediction as image completion~\cite{visualprompt}, Painter learns across dense prediction tasks~\cite{painter}, and SegGPT provides a general context-conditioned segmentation interface~\cite{seggpt}. These approaches establish the annotated example as a flexible specification of the desired output.

uses.context: Recent methods differ in how they turn that example into a query mask. SegIC learns to use foundation-model correspondences as geometric and semantic guidance~\cite{segic}; SINE introduces in-context interaction~\cite{sine}; and VRP-SAM learns a reference-prompt encoder~\cite{vrpsam}. Frozen-model pipelines instead reuse pretrained representations and segmentation priors: PerSAM derives target-specific information from one example~\cite{persam}, and Matcher links general feature matching to promptable segmentation~\cite{matcher}. INSID3 operates directly on DINOv3 features~\cite{insid3}, whereas CG-ICS combines generated concepts, search, and visual exemplars~\cite{cgics}. We compare these last two complete inference systems and then examine their individual processing stages.

uses.context: The chosen reference is itself a source of variation. Good Examples studies example selection~\cite{goodexamples}, UNICL-SAM addresses uncertainty in imperfect examples~\cite{unicl}, and CG-ICS explicitly targets reference robustness~\cite{cgics}. Our reference study measures performance when the query is fixed and the supplied demonstration changes. Cross-domain work provides a complementary perspective: RePRI uses transductive optimization~\cite{repri}, while ABCDFSS adapts feature-processing layers at test time~\cite{abcdfss}. Their adaptation mechanisms differ from the frozen inference evaluated here, motivating a separate domain-transfer analysis.
